statement: In year 3 Quraysh marched with three thousand men; the Muslims took position at Mount Uhud north of Madinah.
He went out with about a thousand; Abdullah ibn Ubayy turned back with a third of the army.
Al-Bara: he placed fifty archers under Abdullah ibn Jubayr and ordered them not to leave their position even if they saw birds snatching the Muslims, nor if they saw victory, until he sent for them.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against both narrations. That they stood on a hill behind the lines is from the Seerah.

statement: Al-Bara: the idolaters fled until their women were seen running up the slope; the archers said 'the spoils'; Abdullah ibn Jubayr reminded them; they left.
notes: Machine-checked. 'Most of them' is from the Seerah (about ten remained).

statement: The Qurayshi cavalry rode around the hill and attacked from behind.
notes: The historians name Khalid ibn al-Walid as its commander.

statement: Sahl ibn Sa'd: his face was wounded, his tooth broken and his helmet crushed on his head; Fatimah washed the wound while Ali poured water from a shield; she burned matting and applied the ash to stop the bleeding.
A cry spread that he had been killed and some lost heart.
Qays saw Talhah's paralysed hand with which he had protected the Prophet at Uhud.
Anas ibn an-Nadr missed Badr and vowed; at Uhud he advanced, told Sa'd ibn Mu'adh he smelled Paradise from Uhud; he was found with over eighty wounds, recognised only by his sister by his fingers.

notes: Machine-checked (Wahshi's account). The mutilation of the dead is not narrated.

statement: Abu Sufyan called out 'a day for the day of Badr, war goes by turns', 'exalted be Hubal' and 'we have al-Uzza'; the Prophet had them answer 'Allah is higher and more majestic' and 'Allah is our protector and you have no protector'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against the full text. The order of Abu Sufyan's phrases is rearranged slightly; reviewer to confirm.

statement: He said: Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.
notes: Number from memory; not machine-checked. The occasion in the narration is a return journey (from Khaybar or Tabuk).
